memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Instead, appoint the Levites to be in charge of the tabernacle of the covenant law—over all its furnishings and everything belonging to it. They are to carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings; they are to take care of it and encamp around it. Whenever the tabernacle is to move, the Levites are to take it down, and whenever the tabernacle is to be set up, the Levites are to do it. Anyone else who approaches it is to be put to death. - Num 1:50-51 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Levites were given the responsibility of caring for the tabernacle — God's dwelling place among His people. They carried it, set it up, took it down, and guarded it. It was holy work, handled with great care and reverence.

The final words are sobering: anyone else who approached it was to be put to death. To us this may sound harsh, but it reveals something important — the holiness of God is not to be treated casually. God was teaching His people that His presence is holy, and that approaching Him carelessly is deadly serious. In a world that had grown used to sin, God was drawing a clear line: holiness matters.

We should not soften this. The seriousness of God's holiness is real. Yet here is the wonder of the gospel: what once meant death for the unauthorised now becomes open access through Christ. Because Jesus died and rose, the way into God's presence is opened for all who come through Him. The curtain that kept people out was torn in two (Heb 10:19-22).

So we approach God today not with careless familiarity, but with reverent confidence — welcomed because of Jesus, yet never forgetting how holy He is.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you take God's holiness seriously in how you approach Him?
- How does Christ's work give you confidence to come to God?
- How can you hold together reverence and confident trust?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy Father, thank You that through Jesus I can come into Your presence. Teach me to approach You with both reverence and confident love. Amen.
